newsitem.title: Singapore: Singapore leaders win multi-million libel damages.
newsitem.headline: Singapore leaders win multi-million libel damages.

text.p: A Singapore court awarded Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong and senior colleagues in his ruling party a record Singapore $8.08 (US$5.65) million in libel damages on Thursday after a political foe called them liars.

Justice Chao Hick Tin said Goh and his colleagues were justified in calling opposition politician Tang Liang Hong "an anti-English education, anti-Christian Chinese chauvinist" who was a danger to Signapore's racial harmony.

Tang had made "malicious" attacks on Goh, former prime minister Lee Kuan Yew and the others which could have affected "their moral authority to govern", including calling them liars over the chauvinsm charge, Chao said in a written judgment.

Goh and his People's Action Party (PAP) colleagues had demanded aggravated damages totalling S$12.9 million, saying Tang had continued to defame them in media interviews he gave after fleeing Singapore saying he had received death threats.
Tang, who fled to the south Malaysian state of Johor after losing a bitterly contested general election fight in January, was not immediately available for comment on the verdict.
He last spoke to reporters from Hong Kong a week ago. Tang told Reuters then he intended to appeal against the award of damages and would bring in a top British lawyer to argue his case.
Tang lost the libel cases in March by failing to turn up to defend himself against charges which mounted almost every time he spoke to the media from Johor, London and Hong Kong.

The comments for which he was sued included an interview with Singapore's Straits Times newspaper, which reported that he claimed "the suits were being used as a politican weapon to squeeze him out of the political area and to 'bury him politically and financially'".
"It is clear that the above quoted remarks constituted another grave attack" on Goh, Lee and their colleagues, Justice Chao said.
Chao made clear that such comments justified aggravated damages.
"This court must show its indignation at the injury inflicted on the plaintiffs," he said in the judgment handed to reporters.
"It cannot be disputed that in terms of aggravation, these 13 cases have no equal," he said.
"The more enormous, outrageous, scandalous or scurrilous the defamation, and/or aggravation, the greater the damages," he added.
Goh, involved in three of the suits against Tang, was awarded S$1.4 million. Lee, involved in five, won the biggest amount -- S$2.3 million.
Chao also hinted that there could be further action to come against Tang, who was heavily criticised by judges for his manoevering during a rash of court hearings leading up to the damages award.
"Whether Mr Tang should be dealt with for scandalising the courts is a matter which may have to be taken up at some other time," Chao said.
Tang was also formally charged last Friday with 33 counts of tax evasion. The court issued an arrest warrant for him.
Tang faces a fine of three times the amount of tax he is accused of evading -- S$211,000 -- plus a fine of S$10,000 on each charge. He could also be jailed for three years on each charge.
